slides.texte_overlay:
things to do instead of
scrolling at night

write tomorrow's list

spend five minutes writing what tomorrow needs from you. your brain stops replaying the day in bed when it knows the next one is already planned and safely on paper.

stretch on the floor

lie on the floor and stretch slowly for ten minutes with dim lights. your body takes the hint that the day is over, and falling asleep becomes noticeably easier.

one lesson in bed

spend 5 minutes learning one calm thing before sleep: a constellation, a famous painting, a myth. you fall asleep thinking about something beautiful instead of something stressful.
slides.texte_sophia:
one lesson in bed

i spend 5 minutes before sleep learning one calm thing: a constellation, a painting, a myth. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and i fall asleep on something beautiful.

slides.texte_overlay:
read paper, not glass

keep a paper book on your pillow so it's the first thing you touch. ten pages of a real book calms your mind in a way that no screen, however dim, ever manages to.

a warm shower

take a warm shower an hour before bed. the drop in body temperature afterwards tells your brain it's time to sleep, and you'll feel heavy and calm by the time you lie down.
